Stonehaven.description: Muddy farming village east of Mt. Kaeloth. About 200 souls. The Stag & Saddle inn anchors the muddy square.

Greymoor.description: Walled market town two days west of Stonehaven on the Old King's Road. Trade hub, temple of Pelor, royal guard contingent, the Blackfeather Inn (thieves'-guild front).

Mt. Kaeloth.description: Volcanic peak. Vorthrax's lair, Stoneheart Hold, is carved into its flank. Approached via the Ashen Pass. Wreathed in smoke.

The Whispering Woods.description: Dense forest north of Greymoor. Hides the elven enclave of Sylvanloft, bandits, and worse things deeper in.

Sylvanloft.description: Hidden elven enclave. Lady Sirenne is the matriarch. Holds the Tear of Aelin.

The Ruins of Eldrath.description: Sacked elven city. Haunted. Contains a magical archive.

Aurelion.description: Royal capital. A week's ride south of Greymoor. Walled, prosperous, insulated from the dragon's terror.

Garrick Stoneward.personality: Gruff ex-soldier. Lost his son to Vorthrax's sacrifice three years ago. Quietly helpful to anyone who'll fight the dragon.
Garrick Stoneward.notes:
First met when Benito entered the Stag & Saddle at dusk. Acknowledged Benito with a nod and offered ale or a room.
Benito claimed a close friend lost a child to the dragon and he seeks justice. Garrick opened up about losing his son Tam (8 years old) three years ago. Shared that this year's sacrifice is Elspeth, the miller's six-year-old daughter, due in two months. Advised Benito to seek out Old Wynn for knowledge of Stoneheart Hold's tunnels—warned Wynn won't help for free.

Mira Vell.personality: Shrewd, fair. Knows everyone's business. Sells mundane gear at fair prices.

Captain Hadrik Brenn.personality: Honest and weary. Recruiting heroes for the dragon bounty. Has watched many ride out and not return.

Old Wynn.personality: Eccentric, possibly drunk, knows more than he lets on. Grudge against the elves of Sylvanloft.
Old Wynn.notes: Knows the layout of pre-fall Stoneheart Hold.

Lady Sirenne.personality: Cold, proud, distrusts humans. Lost her sister at Eldrath.
Lady Sirenne.notes: Custodian of the Tear of Aelin.

The Crimson Shadow.description: Seek justice against Vorthrax the Crimson for the children he has taken. The miller's daughter Elspeth is due as tribute in two months. Garrick suggested seeking Old Wynn, a hedge wizard south of Stonehaven, who knows the layout of Stoneheart Hold.

content.text: lets get an ale

You rap your knuckles on the bar's worn surface. Garrick Stoneward glances up from the tankard he's wiping, gives you a once-over with those tired soldier's eyes, and reaches for a clay pitcher without a word.

"Copper for the ale," he says, setting a foaming tankard in front of you. The brew is dark, with a head the color of old parchment. "Two silver if you want a room for the night. Supper's included either way—rabbit stew tonight."

The common room is quiet at this hour. A pair of farmers mutter over a dice game in the corner. Near the hearth, an old woman knits something gray and shapeless, humming tunelessly. The fire crackles, throwing dancing shadows across the low beams.

Through the window, the last light of dusk paints Mt. Kaeloth's distant peak in shades of blood and ash. A thin tendril of smoke—or is it steam?—curls from the summit, barely visible against the darkening sky.

Garrick follows your gaze for a moment, then looks away. His jaw tightens.

"You passing through," he asks, "or staying a while?"

You slide two silver coins across the bar with a flourish, letting your fingers linger just a moment—a gesture you perfected in the courts of your youth, though you'd used it then to charm visiting dignitaries out of their secrets.

"Staying a while," you say, offering Garrick your most disarming smile. "A village like this, good ale, honest folk—seems like the kind of place worth getting to know."

content.text: Gold changed by -2 (Paid for a room at the Stag & Saddle (2 silver)). Player has 22gp.

Garrick pockets the silver and grunts. He doesn't seem *un*friendly, exactly, but your courtly charm slides off him like water off oiled leather. He's seen too much, you suspect—lost too much—to be won over by a pretty smile and honeyed words.

"Room's up the stairs, second on the left," he says, already turning back to his tankards. "Stew'll be ready in an hour."

He pauses, though. Something in his posture shifts—just slightly. He glances at you sidelong.

"You're elven," he says. It's not a question. "Don't see many of your kind passing through anymore. Not since—" He stops himself, shakes his head. "Well. Not since."

He sets another tankard under the tap, filling it for no one in particular. His hands are steady, but there's a tension in his shoulders.

"You here about the dragon? Or running from something else?"

The question hangs in the smoky air. The old woman by the fire has stopped humming. The farmers' dice have gone quiet.
taking day by day, ive heard about the dragon

You take a long pull of your ale, letting the silence stretch just enough to feel natural.

"Taking it day by day," you say, setting the tankard down. "But aye, I've heard about the dragon. Hard not to, even on the roads. Vorthrax." You let the name sit there, watching Garrick's reaction. "They say he demands tribute. Gold. Cattle." You pause. "Children."

Garrick's knuckles go white around the tankard he's holding. For a moment you think he might shatter it. Then he sets it down carefully—too carefully—and exhales through his nose.

"They say true."

He braces both hands on the bar and looks at you properly for the first time. There's no warmth in his eyes, but there's something else now. A flicker of desperate, weary hope, quickly smothered.

"Three years ago, it was my boy. Tam. Eight years old." His voice is flat, rehearsed—like he's told himself this story so many times the edges have worn smooth. "Drew the short straw. Whole village watched him walk up the Ashen Pass. Didn't even cry. Brave little fool."

He straightens, rolls his shoulders like he's shaking something off.

"This year it's the miller's daughter. Elspeth. Six years old. Lot's been drawn already. Two months out." He fixes you with a hard stare. "So when you say you've *heard* about the dragon—what exactly are you planning to *do* about what you've heard?"

The farmers have given up all pretense of their dice game. The old woman's knitting needles have gone still. Everyone in the Stag & Saddle is listening now.
a close friend of mine has also lost a child to the dragon. i aim to seek justice for my friend

The words land heavy in the quiet room. Garrick studies your face—searching for the lie, perhaps, or the bravado that usually comes before young fools ride off to die. Whatever he finds there makes him exhale slowly, some of the tension bleeding from his shoulders.

"Justice," he repeats, like he's tasting the word. "Been a long time since anyone called it that. Most who come through talk about glory. The bounty. A barony from the king." He shakes his head. "They don't last long."

He reaches beneath the bar and produces a second tankard, fills it from the tap, and raises it toward you.

"To your friend's child, then. And to mine." He drinks deep, then wipes his mouth with the back of his hand. "I won't insult you by saying you'll die up there. You know the odds well as anyone. But if you're serious..."

He leans in, lowering his voice. The firelight catches the old scar running along his jaw.

"There's a hedge wizard lives in a tower south of here. Old Wynn. Madder than a sack of cats and twice as prickly, but he *knows* things. Served with the dwarves of Stoneheart Hold before it fell. Knows the tunnels, the traps, the old ways in." Garrick's eyes flick toward the mountain's silhouette in the window. "Dragon didn't take the front gate. Flew in through the peak and worked his way down. Means the dwarven defenses might still be intact—pointed the wrong direction, but intact."

He straightens, voice returning to normal volume.

"Wynn won't help for free. Never does. But if you're clever—and you look clever—you might find a way to loosen his tongue."

He raises his tankard once more before draining it.

"Room's paid for. Stew's on the house tonight." A ghost of a smile crosses his weathered face—the first you've seen. "Get some rest. If you're heading to Wynn's tower tomorrow, you'll want your wits about you. The old bastard loves his riddles."
thank you, ill need all the help i can get . then lets go sleep

You clasp Garrick's forearm in thanks—a soldier's gesture he seems to appreciate—and drain the last of your ale. The rabbit stew arrives shortly after, hearty and well-seasoned, and you eat in comfortable silence while the common room slowly empties.

When you finally climb the creaking stairs to your room, the night has fully settled over Stonehaven. Your chamber is small but clean: a straw mattress with a wool blanket, a washbasin, a single window facing south. Through it, you can just make out a faint flicker of light in the distant darkness—Old Wynn's tower, perhaps, burning the midnight oil.

You check the door's lock out of habit—a rogue's instinct—wedge your pack beneath the bed, and settle in with your shortsword within arm's reach.

Sleep comes easier than expected. The ale helps. So does the strange comfort of having a purpose, however dangerous.

You wake to pale dawn light filtering through the window and the distant crow of a rooster. The smell of woodsmoke and frying eggs drifts up from below. Your body feels rested, your mind sharp.

Through the window, Mt. Kaeloth looms against the brightening sky, its peak wreathed in the same thin curl of smoke. Closer, to the south, you can see a smudge of gray stone rising above the treeline—Old Wynn's tower, perhaps a mile or two's walk through the fields.

The day stretches before you, full of possibility.
